issues.detail: The Greek 'οταν δε ειπη' (when He said) is rendered as 'nhưng khi nói rằng' (but when saying that). The Vietnamese adds a contrastive conjunction ('nhưng') and changes the subject of the verb 'nói' (saying) from a specific action by 'He' (God/Christ) to a general statement, losing the specific attribution of the speech.

The Greek 'οταν δε ειπη' implies a specific instance of 'when He said'. The Vietnamese 'nhưng khi nói rằng' softens this into a general condition or a hypothetical, potentially leading the reader to miss that this refers to a specific declaration.
